name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
blurb: Senegal River delta wetland where millions of birds stop after crossing the Sahara.

tip.title: Crash the fish
tip.text: Set Nile tilapia to -100% and watch pelicans, herons and crocodiles lose their main food, then the animals that eat them.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong sun in a hot, dry region drives plant growth wherever floodwater keeps the ground wet.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead reeds, floating plants and animal remains, returning nutrients to the water and mud.
Tall emergent reed. Cattails (typhas) proliferated in the delta after the Diama Dam began operating.
Tall grass of wetland edges whose dense stands shelter nesting waterbirds; it has spread since the dam.

nodes.name: White Egyptian lotus
nodes.desc: Floating-leaved water lily of the sanctuary pools, recorded near the park.
The best-recorded mammal near the sanctuary; it grazes and roots, and GloBI records it eating water lettuce.
Widespread African freshwater fish that eats plants and algae; a main food of fish-eating birds and crocodiles.
Hunts rodents, birds, eggs and reptiles; GloBI holds records of it eating many of the local birds.
Opportunistic canid that hunts rodents and hares and also scavenges carcasses.
Large lizard of riversides that eats fish, eggs, frogs, small mammals and carrion.
Wading bird that stalks fish, amphibians and small rodents in shallows.
Nests in the sanctuary; hunts fish, often in groups that herd fish together. Pelicans are among its most visible birds.
Raptor that quarters reedbeds and wetlands, hunting waterbirds, small mammals and other prey; the best-recorded bird near the park.
Large constrictor; GloBI records it eating Nile monitors, and it also takes rodents.
